info.description: HTTP API for uploading, reading, searching and questioning Documents. Every route except the probes needs an API key.
info.title: Trelis API

post.description: Retrieves the Documents the caller can read, then asks models.chat for one answer that cites the retrieved Chunks. Sources are numbered [1]..[n] in retrieval order; each claim is cited with its source numbers in square brackets, the answer text keeps the valid markers, and citations lists each cited source once in order of first appearance. A marker outside 1..n is removed from the text and never cited; a marker inside Markdown code or a Markdown link is left untouched and never cited. When retrieval finds nothing the answer is a fixed sentence in the question's language and no chat call is made. debug adds the retrieved Chunks (exactly as POST /retrieve answers them), the trace with a final generate step, and the token usage of every model call, including a query rewrite. With conversation_id, the Conversation's last five turns are carried into retrieval and this question and the cleaned answer are recorded as its next turn; naming query_rewrite then rewrites a follow-up into one standalone query before any technique searches, and the raw question is still what the no-source answer and the recorded turn keep. The Conversation must belong to the caller: an unknown or foreign id is 404 before any retrieval or model call. Without conversation_id the answer has no history and records nothing. With Accept: text/event-stream the answer streams Answer Events as Server-Sent Events instead: id is the per-answer seq and event is started {"answer_id"}, token {"text"} per model delta, citation {"marker","chunk_id","document_id"} after the text, then done {"answer","finish_reason","debug"?}; an error {"message"} replaces done when generation fails or the turn cannot be recorded, and both are terminal. The chat stream is opened before the SSE response, so a provider rejection is the same JSON 502. A dropped client resumes at GET /answers/{answer_id}/events with Last-Event-ID. Malformed JSON, unknown fields, invalid values and the retrieval rules are 400; a body over 64 KiB is 413; without models.chat the route answers 503 before any retrieval, and retrieval's own 503 (models.embedding for dense, models.rerank for rerank, models.chat for query rewrite) passes through; a model provider's rejection of a retrieval or opening the chat stream (its credentials, credit, permission or rate limit) is 502 and names the model role in its message, and any other model failure is a generic 500. Every one of these failures answers the JSON error before the SSE headers.
post.summary: Answer a question from readable Documents

parameters.description: The query, how many Chunks to retrieve, which Retrieval Techniques to run, the Conversation to continue and whether to return the debug object
parameters.name: request

200.description: The JSON answer when Accept does not ask for text/event-stream; otherwise Server-Sent Events: started, token..., citation..., then done or error

400.description: Body that is not one JSON object, an unknown field or wrong value type, a blank or too-long query, an out-of-range top_k or an invalid retrieval_config

404.description: The conversation_id is unknown or belongs to another Principal; answered before any retrieval or model call

500.description: Internal server error, including a Conversation turn that could not be recorded; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

502.description: A model provider rejected the call because of its credentials, credit, permission or rate limit (an embedding, rerank or chat status 401, 402, 403 or 429); the message names the model role, never the provider's body

503.description: models.chat is not configured, or retrieval is unavailable (models.embedding for dense, models.rerank for rerank, models.chat for query rewrite)

get.description: Streams a Pipeline Answer's Answer Events as Server-Sent Events, starting after Last-Event-ID. Each frame's id is the event's seq within the answer and event is started, token, citation, done or error. started carries {"answer_id"}, token {"text"} (the raw model delta), citation {"marker","chunk_id","document_id"} once per cited source in first-appearance order, and done {"answer","finish_reason","debug"?} or error {"message"} ends the stream. Only the Principal who asked for the answer may resume it; any other caller gets the same 404 as for an unknown or expired answer ID.

parameters.description: Seq of the last event the client saw; only later events are sent
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

200.description: Server-Sent Events, one frame per answer event; the stream ends after done or error

404.description: No answer stream with that ID, it expired, or it belongs to another Principal

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Returns the Chunk, without its embedding, when the caller can read its Document. A Chunk that does not exist and one whose Document the caller cannot read answer the same 404, so a Restricted Document's existence is not revealed.

400.description: ID that is not a UUID

404.description: No readable Chunk with that ID

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

post.description: Creates a Conversation owned by the caller for a series of follow-up questions. The body is empty or an empty JSON object. Ask a question in it with POST /answer and its conversation_id; the answer carries the last five turns into retrieval and records the new turn.

400.description: A body that is not an empty JSON object

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Returns the caller's Conversation with its turns in seq order: each turn's seq, raw question, rewritten_query when a query rewrite ran, cleaned answer and created_at. turns is [] when the Conversation has no turns, never null. A turn whose source Documents are no longer all readable to the caller keeps its seq, question and created_at, answers answer:"" with withheld:true, and drops rewritten_query; source_document_ids is never exposed. A Conversation the caller does not own, an unknown id and a malformed id all answer the same 404 body.
get.summary: Read a Conversation and its turns

404.description: No Conversation with that id belongs to the caller; a malformed id answers the same body

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Returns one page of the Documents the caller can read, newest first, without Access Lists. A page or page_size of 0, or either left out, takes the default: page 1 and page_size 20.

parameters.description: Page number, 1-based; 0 or absent means the default of 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size; 0 or absent means the default of 20
parameters.name: page_size

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

post.description: Uploads one file as a new Document. "principals" and "groups" each name a comma-separated list added to the Access List; the uploader is always on it. Answers 409 when the caller already uploaded the same content.

parameters.description: Comma-separated Principal names for the Access List
parameters.name: principals

parameters.description: Comma-separated Group names for the Access List
parameters.name: groups

400.description: Malformed upload, unknown Principal or Group, or unsupported file type

409.description: The caller already uploaded this content

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Returns the Document, or 404 when it does not exist or the caller cannot read it, so a Restricted Document's existence is not revealed. Only the owner sees its Access List.

404.description: No readable Document with that ID

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

delete.description: Only the Document's owner may delete it. Removes the Document and everything derived from it, cancels its ingest and, once the row is gone, removes every object it stored. A reader who is not the owner gets 403; a caller who cannot read the Document gets 404, the same as for one that does not exist.

403.description: The caller can read the Document but is not its owner

404.description: No readable Document with that ID

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Streams the Document's Ingest Events as Server-Sent Events while the caller can read it. Each frame's id is the event's seq within the Document, event is parse_started, parse_finished, embed_batch_finished, upload_replaced, completed or failed, and data is {"document_id","upload_id","type","detail","created_at"}. detail is {"attempt"} for parse_started, {"chunks"} for parse_finished, {"from","to","chunks"} for embed_batch_finished, {"upload_id"} for upload_replaced, {"reason"} for failed, and {} for completed. Reconnecting with Last-Event-ID replays the events after that seq, then carries on live. After a re-upload the stream passes an older upload's completed or failed event, then its upload_replaced event, and ends at the current upload's completed or failed. It also ends when the Document is gone or no longer readable, when the client disconnects, when the server shuts down, or after 30 minutes so a Document stuck in processing cannot hold it forever; reconnecting with Last-Event-ID loses nothing.

parameters.description: Per-Document seq of the last event the client saw; only later events are sent
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

200.description: Server-Sent Events, one frame per Ingest Event; the stream ends after the current upload's completed or failed, or after 30 minutes

404.description: No readable Document with that ID

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Streams the file as an attachment, never rendered in the API's origin. The Content-Disposition header names it and Content-Length gives its size.

404.description: No readable Document with that ID

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

put.description: Replaces the Document's Source File with the uploaded one, under a new upload ID, and starts ingesting the new upload. The Access List is unchanged. Only the owner may replace it; the access and owner checks run before the body is read. Answers 409 with the earlier Document when the caller already has a Document with the same content. A concurrent re-upload answers 412; a concurrent delete answers 404. The old Chunks are removed before this returns.

400.description: Malformed upload, invalid Document ID or unsupported file type

403.description: The caller can read the Document but is not its owner

404.description: No readable Document with that ID

409.description: The caller already has a Document with this content

412.description: A concurrent re-upload changed the Document; retry

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Answers 200 while the process is serving requests, whatever its dependencies are.
Returns the Principal the API key belongs to, with its Groups, as the bare Principal rather than the response envelope.

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

get.description: Probes Postgres, object storage, Neo4j and Temporal concurrently. Answers 200 when all are up, 503 when any is down.

post.description: Runs every candidate Retrieval Technique named in retrieval_config (dense and/or bm25) over the Documents the caller can read. One technique answers in its own order with its own score; several run concurrently over max(top_k, 50) candidates each and are fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, score = the sum of 1/(rrf_k + rank) over the lists that carry the Chunk, then cut to top_k with equal fused scores ordered by chunk_id. rrf_k defaults to 60 and must be between 1 and 1000; it has no effect with one technique. Naming rerank adds a second stage: the candidate pool (the single list or the fused list, cut to rerank_candidates) is scored once by the rerank model, ordered by that score with ties by chunk_id; rerank cannot run alone. rerank_candidates defaults to 50, must be between 1 and 100 and at least top_k, and has no effect without rerank. Naming parent_child adds a final stage: each matched Chunk is replaced by its Parent Chunk, several matched Chunks of one Parent Chunk collapse into the position of the best-ranked matched Chunk, and a Chunk with no Parent Chunk stands alone; chunk_id, document_id, seq, score, scores and ranks stay the best-ranked matched Chunk's, content and context_header become the Parent Chunk's, and parent_chunk_id names it (absent for a standalone Chunk). Without rerank parent_child searches max(top_k, 50) deep; with rerank the pool stays rerank_candidates and the cut to top_k happens after the collapse. Naming query_rewrite adds a first stage: when the request carries Conversation History, which POST /answer fills, the chat role rewrites the latest question into one standalone query and every technique, and rerank, searches with it; the trace then starts with rewrite_query carrying rewritten_query and the call's usage. Without history no model call is made, so POST /retrieve accepts query_rewrite and never calls a model. query_rewrite cannot run alone. Every result carries the score and 1-based rank of each technique whose list carried it, plus the rerank score and rank when it ran. A bm25 request needs no embedding model. A caller who can read nothing gets 200 with an empty results list. Malformed JSON, unknown fields, invalid values, an unknown or duplicate technique, a config whose only techniques are stages (query_rewrite, rerank, parent_child), an out-of-range rrf_k or rerank_candidates are 400; a body over 64 KiB is 413; without models.embedding, a dense request is 503, without models.rerank a request naming rerank is 503, and without models.chat a request naming query_rewrite is 503. A model provider's rejection of the call (its credentials, credit, permission or rate limit) is 502 and names the model role in its message; any other model failure is a generic 500.

parameters.description: The query, how many Chunks to return, which Retrieval Techniques to run (dense, bm25, query_rewrite, rerank, parent_child), the RRF constant and the rerank candidate pool
parameters.name: request

400.description: Body that is not one JSON object, an unknown field or wrong value type, a blank or too-long query, an out-of-range top_k or an invalid retrieval_config (an unknown or duplicate technique, only stage techniques such as query_rewrite, rerank or parent_child, an rrf_k outside 1..1000, or a rerank_candidates outside 1..100 or below top_k)

500.description: Internal server error; a failed API key check answers the router's error body instead

502.description: A model provider rejected the call because of its credentials, credit, permission or rate limit (an embedding or rerank status 401, 402, 403 or 429); the message names the model role, never the provider's body

503.description: models.embedding is not configured so dense cannot run, models.rerank is not configured so rerank cannot run, or models.chat is not configured so query_rewrite cannot run (bm25 alone still works)

usage.description: Usage is the chat call's token accounting; zeros when no call was made.

conversation_id.description:
ConversationID asks the answer to carry the Conversation's last turns
into retrieval and to record this question and answer as its next turn;
nil answers without history and records nothing. The Conversation must
belong to the caller, and an unknown or foreign one is a 404 before any
retrieval or model call.

debug.description:
Debug asks the answer to carry the retrieved Chunks, the trace and the
chat call's token usage; false leaves the debug object out entirely.

query.description: Query is the question to find Chunks for.

retrieval_config.description:
RetrievalConfig is the combination of techniques to run; nil means
dense alone.

top_k.description:
TopK is how many Chunks to return; nil means the default. An explicit
0 is invalid, so a client that sends it learns it is out of range
instead of silently getting the default.

citations.description: Citations is never null: an answer with no source cites nothing.

debug.description:
Debug is present only when the request set debug; nil leaves the key
out.

content.description: Content is the source text of the Chunk

context_header.description:
ContextHeader is context that is not in the source at the offsets,
such as a heading breadcrumb or a repeated table header

end_offset.description: EndOffset is the rune just past the last one in Content

seq.description: Seq orders the Chunks of one Document, starting at 0

start_offset.description: StartOffset is the first rune of the Document's Markdown in Content

chunk_id.description: ChunkID is the retrieved Chunk the marker stands for.

document_id.description: DocumentID is the Document that Chunk belongs to.

marker.description: Marker is the source number the answer text cites, e.g. 2 for [2].

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the Conversation was created.

id.description: ID identifies the Conversation on every route that reads it.

turns.description: Turns are its turns in Seq order; it is never null in a read answer.

answer.description: Answer is the cleaned answer text, exactly as the answer returned it.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the turn was recorded.

question.description: Question is the raw question the caller asked.

rewritten_query.description:
RewrittenQuery is the standalone query a query rewrite produced and
retrieval searched with, or nil when no rewrite ran. It is the query
actually used, so a rewrite that fell back to the raw question stores
that.

seq.description: Seq is the Conversation's own sequence number, starting at 1.

withheld.description:
Withheld is true when any source Document is no longer readable to the
caller: Answer is empty, RewrittenQuery is nil, and only Seq, Question
and CreatedAt are shown.

access_list.description:
AccessList is filled in only for the owner, so other readers do not
learn who else can read the Document.

file_hash.description: File hash of the Document: hex SHA-256 of its content

file_size.description: File size of the Document in bytes

file_type.description: File type of the Document: its lower-case extension

parse_error.description:
ParseError is why the last parse failed; empty unless ParseStatus is
failed. It names no file name or Document text.

title.description: Title of the Document; the file name at upload

updated_at.description: Last updated time of the Document

chunk_id.description: ChunkID is the result's chunk_id, the best-ranked matched Chunk.

matched_chunk_ids.description:
MatchedChunkIDs is every matched Chunk that collapsed into the result,
in rank order; the first is ChunkID.

parent_chunk_id.description:
ParentChunkID is the Parent Chunk that supplied the content; nil when
the result is a Chunk with no Parent Chunk.

rerank_candidates.description:
RerankCandidates is how many Chunks the first stage hands to the
reranker; nil means the default. It is accepted and ignored when the
list does not name the rerank technique.

rrf_k.description:
RRFK is the Reciprocal Rank Fusion constant k; nil means the default.
It only affects a request that runs more than one technique, so it is
accepted and ignored for a single one.

techniques.description:
Techniques is the set of Retrieval Techniques to run, without
duplicates. More than one candidate technique makes the request a
fusion: each runs over the readable Documents and their lists are
combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. query_rewrite rewrites the
question first when the request carries Conversation History; rerank
reorders whatever the candidate techniques found; parent_child then
replaces the ordered Chunks with their Parent Chunks.

query.description: Query is the question to find Chunks for.

retrieval_config.description:
RetrievalConfig is the combination of techniques to run; nil means
dense alone.

top_k.description:
TopK is how many Chunks to return; nil means the default. An explicit
0 is invalid, so a client that sends it learns it is out of range
instead of silently getting the default.

chunk_id.description:
ChunkID, DocumentID and Seq are the best-ranked matched Chunk's, so a
citation or GET /chunks/{id} still reaches a real Chunk.

content.description:
Content and ContextHeader are the Parent Chunk's when the request
expanded to parents, else the Chunk's own.

parent_chunk_id.description:
ParentChunkID is the Parent Chunk the content came from; it is absent
when the Chunk stands alone.

candidates.description:
Candidate count fields below keep their pointer shape so a step that
has no count leaves the field out.

Candidates is how many Chunks the step returned: the search step's own
matches, the distinct Chunks a fuse step combined, the pool size sent
to the reranker, or the results the expand_parents step produced before
the cut.

duration_ms.description: DurationMS is how long the step took, in milliseconds.

expanded.description:
Expanded says which Chunks collapsed into which result, one entry per
returned result in result order, on the expand_parents step. It is a
pointer so an expand step with no results still answers expanded: []
while every other step leaves the field out.

model.description:
Model is the embedding, rerank or chat model, on the step that called
one.

rewritten_query.description:
RewrittenQuery is the query the techniques searched with, on the
rewrite_query step: the model's reply, or the raw question when the
reply was blank or too long.

step.description: Step names what ran, e.g. TraceStepEmbedQuery.

technique.description:
Technique is the Retrieval Technique the step belongs to, or
RetrievalTechniqueRRF on the fuse step.

usage.description: Usage is the chat call's token accounting on the rewrite_query step.

bearerAuth.description: Paste "Bearer <key>", with a key from `trelis admin key create <principal>` (`go run ./cmd/server admin key create <principal>` in dev).
bearerAuth.name: Authorization
